deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 1 of the July–August 1967 notes 'Anneaux simpliciaux canoniques et modules stratifiés'. These are preparatory notes for the Nov–Dec 1967 IHES lectures 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', later written up in Dix exposés. The previous page sets up the following. X→S is smooth. X^{[n]} is the (n+1)-fold fibre product, and its formal completion along the diagonal is taken. Its structure sheaf P^n is a pro-ring on |X|. As n varies, these give a cosimplicial O_X-algebra P^*, the sheaves of principal parts of infinite order, with P^0 = O_X.

This page makes three points.

(1) Caution. P^* is a cosimplicial ring under O_X, but not a cosimplicial O_X-algebra in the naive sense. The two coface maps d^0, d^1 : O_X = P^0 ⇉ P^1 differ in general. So P^1 carries two distinct O_X-algebra structures, the left and right ones (p_1^*, p_2^*). These are what the next page uses: P^i ⊗ M via the 'right/external' structure, leading to stratifications as descent-type data.

(2) The shift (décalage) SP. It is defined by (SP)^i = P^{i+1}, or functorially, viewing a cosimplicial object as a functor on nonempty finite (ordered) sets, by (SP)(I) = P(I ⊔ e), where e is a point. The inclusion I → I ⊔ e gives a natural map α : P^* → (SP)^*, that is, α^i : P^i → P^{i+1}. This is the standard device for producing an extra codegeneracy, i.e. a contracting homotopy. The shifted object is homotopy equivalent to its degree-0 part, which yields linearization and Poincaré-lemma type acyclicity statements (the de Rham complex of P^1 resolving O_X, the Čech–Alexander complex).

(3) Affine example. Take S = Spec k and X = Spec A, with the diagonal an immersion (e.g. X separated of finite type). Passing to sections, Γ P^i is identified with A^{⊗_k (i+1)}, with the usual Amitsur/bar cofaces and codegeneracies. In this picture α^i(x_0⊗…⊗x_i) = x_0⊗…⊗x_i⊗1, i.e. insertion of 1 in the new last slot.

The page is purely set-up for the cosimplicial / descent approach to stratified modules and crystals.
errors: Γ P^i should be the completion of A^{⊗(i+1)} along the kernel of the multiplication map (the diagonal ideal), or the corresponding pro-object. Writing simply A^{⊗(i+1)} drops the formal completion defined on the previous page. This is probably deliberate shorthand or an illustration.
The hypothesis that X → X×_S X be an immersion is automatic for schemes. What separatedness adds is that it is a closed immersion, so the parenthetical condition is loosely stated.

α (adding the point e at the end) is the extra coface of the décalage. On SP it is a morphism of cosimplicial objects only when SP is given the shifted structure that forgets the last coface/codegeneracy. This is implicit but not stated.

ideas.what: Cosimplicial ring of formal neighbourhoods of the diagonal (principal parts of infinite order); left and right O_X-structures on P^1
ideas.modern_name: Infinitesimal groupoid / Čech–Alexander or Amitsur cosimplicial algebra; jets with left and right structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (EGA IV 16, Crystals and de Rham cohomology 1968); Berthelot 1974
ideas.where_published: EGA IV §16; 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968)
